content_voiceover: This flowchart presents a practical clinical algorithm for choosing anticoagulation in cancer associated VTE, drawn from a Nature Reviews Disease Primers article. Starting at the top with a diagnosis of cancer associated VTE, you work through a series of yes or no questions. First, does the patient have gastrointestinal, hepatic, or renal function impairment? If yes, low molecular weight heparin is preferred, since direct oral anticoagulants rely on adequate GI absorption and renal or hepatic clearance. If no, move to the next question, is the patient on a potent CYP3A4 or P glycoprotein inducer or inhibitor? Many chemotherapy agents and targeted therapies interact with these pathways, and if there's a significant interaction, again LMWH is preferred to avoid unpredictable anticoagulant levels. If no significant interaction, the next branch asks about high bleeding risk, for example thrombocytopenia or an unresected mucosal cancer like a GI or bladder tumor that could bleed. If bleeding risk is high, LMWH is again favored. Only if the patient clears all three of these checkpoints, meaning no organ dysfunction, no significant drug interaction, and no high bleeding risk, do we prefer a direct oral anticoagulant, specifically apixaban, edoxaban, or rivaroxaban. Regardless of which agent is chosen, the patient is reassessed every three months, and anticoagulation may be stopped if there's no evidence of active cancer and no ongoing cancer therapy.
keypoints: LMWH preferred if GI, hepatic, or renal dysfunction present
LMWH preferred with significant CYP3A4 or P-glycoprotein drug interactions
LMWH preferred in high bleeding risk, e.g. thrombocytopenia or unresected mucosal cancer
DOACs apixaban, edoxaban, or rivaroxaban preferred if none of the above apply
Reassess every three months, consider stopping if cancer is inactive and untreated
keypoint_voiceover: Choice of anticoagulant in cancer associated VTE follows a stepwise check for organ dysfunction, drug interactions, and bleeding risk, favoring LMWH when any are present and a DOAC otherwise, with reassessment every three months.
